conventions.convention: Signal dimension d is at least 1; measurement count m may be zero. Measurement labels are [m]={1,...,m}, whereas signal coordinates are indexed by k<d. Zero and repeated measurement vectors and nonspanning families are allowed.

Real recovery identifies exactly x and -x, including the singleton class of zero. The quotient metric is min{||x-z||₂,||x+z||₂}; amplitudes and intensities have identical fibers. The empty data space is a singleton with zero metric.

The complement property quantifies over every subset of measurement labels, including empty and full subsets; the empty span is {0}. Full spark is defined only for m≥d and requires independence of every d distinct labels.

Canonical signs have s₁=+1, with +1 ordered before -1; m=0 has one empty pattern. P counts patterns and L counts right-hand-side solves after one SVD. Zero budgets return no candidates and budget-exhausted. Noisy mode scores squared amplitude residual, preserves the earlier candidate on ties, and ignores the feasibility tolerance.
Exact-mode completeness requires zero tolerance and complete enumeration. Positive tolerance screens least-squares affine families; it does not enumerate every vector within tolerance.
The finite Fourier example uses the unnormalised C₃ transform with ω=(-1-i√3)/2, translation f(n-1), and reflection f(-n).

The complex counterexample explicitly uses a pairing conjugate-linear in its measurement-vector argument and linear in its signal argument, and identifies signals by arbitrary unit-modulus global phase.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite family in real dimension d≥1, including m=0, the intensity map is injective on global-sign classes if and only if every partition of measurement labels has at least one side spanning the ambient space.

The procedure terminates within P, L and N_m signed solves. Complete exact enumeration at zero tolerance returns exactly the intensity inverse image modulo sign; complete noisy enumeration returns a global minimizer of the squared amplitude residual. An early incumbent minimizes that objective among processed candidates only.

The sign relation is an equivalence relation, d± is a metric on its quotient, the specified data spaces are metric spaces, both measurement maps are well defined, and amplitude and intensity maps are injective simultaneously.

Every real family with m≤2d-2 fails phase retrieval; a full-spark real family with m≥2d-1 performs phase retrieval. At m=2d-1, moment-curve vectors at distinct real nodes attain this count for every d≥1.
For d≥1, det(t_j^(i-1))=∏_{p<q}(t_q-t_p); consequently the d moment-curve vectors at distinct real nodes are linearly independent.

Enumerate canonical signed square-root targets subject to pattern and solve budgets, compute their minimum-norm least-squares candidates, and return qualified affine families in exact mode or the least amplitude-residual visited candidate in noisy mode.

concerns.concern: The Statement refuted specifies the dot product as “u₁v₁+u₂v₂”, whereas def-ip-real-frame-phase-retrieval explicitly fixes signal coordinates k<d. For d=2 those coordinates are 0 and 1. The intended axis computation is sound, but the example needs an explicit local relabeling or consistent zero-based coordinate subscripts.

The Example writes its intensity map as “[x]↦(x₁²,x₂²,(x₁+x₂)²)”. Its cited model explicitly uses zero-based signal coordinates k<d, so x₂ is not a coordinate of that model's R². The tuple calculations are sound under a one-based relabeling, which is not stated here.

Proof 4.1 invokes the complement property without explicitly assuming it for the first implication. Proof 5.1 then says “The forward implication is proved in step 4.1”, although the Statement orders injectivity before the complement property and 4.1 proves complement property ⇒ injectivity. The intended two-direction argument is otherwise complete.

alerts.finding: In this published supplier, Proof 3.1 says “steps 2.1-2.1 identify that exact solution set with the same affine family.” The two directions establishing that family are actually steps 2.1 and 2.2; the closing tags already cite both. This is a duplicated endpoint in the prose locator.

seams_checked.note: The phase-retrieval definition cites the supplier's forward-map, target-class and identifiability definitions faithfully. Its sign quotient is onto, and injectivity of the induced intensity map is exactly identifiability modulo global sign. The supplier makes no converse citation or stronger phase-retrieval claim.

This declared page prerequisite is contextual: no assigned item invokes its unbounded Hilbert-space pseudoinverse, closed-range theorem or Picard criterion.
